page.layout: One column of running text, with one marginal note in the right margin beside the line "Ufus fervetur verus". The division heading "RESPONSIO." stands centred in the middle of the page, and the text continues below it. No note in the left margin. The page number and running head stand at the head of the page.

main_text.p: Studium, ut experientia ipsa declarat, frigescit atque exstinguitur; dum tant[?] homines jam reipsa ejustos[?] esse, quia licet omnium suorum peccatorum universa ma[?] divina justitia perfoluta fuerint.

Item ajunt: Ut per speciem sanctimonia vitae bilienda[?], omnis vera sanctitas convelleretur: humani generis hoste versutissimo persuasi prudentes, imputationem justitia Christi exstitarunt; per quam scilicet nobis, licet adhuc [?]catis servissimus, ea sanctimonia adscribatur.

Clamant itaque adversarii, doctrinam de merito & satisfactione Christi, aut prorsus tollere, aut vehementer saltem impedire studium sanc-monia, sine qua nemo Deum videbit, Heb.12. dum nimirum homines persuasi, pro omnibus peccatis Deo planissime esse satisfactum, opinantur jam se vere justos esse alienâ justitiâ, nec posse gratia Dei excidere, quamvis indulgeant [?]eleribus: nec interea animadvertunt, Deum omnino exigere conditionem resipiscentiae, sine qua omnia[?] peccata remitti possunt. Jes.1.16.17.18. Zech.18.21.22. Actor.2.20. & cap.5.19.
main_text.head: RESPONSIO.
main_text.p: Usus servetur verus, tollatur abusus. Ut dissentimus ab illis, qui ita resipiscentiam & vitae sanctimoniam urgent, ut meritum & satisfactionem Jesu Chri-sti

page.notes: Marginal note on the right, beside "Ufus fervetur verus": "Responsio." Printed in italics in the margin. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: the word before "homines" (likely a partial word cut at the line), "ejustos", "ma" (a partial word at the start of the line), "scatis", "eleribus" (the word at the start of the line is not clear), and "omnia". The page number is read as 31 from the header and is marked [?]. The catchword "pro" is printed at the right foot. "Heb.12." may be "Heb.13." and is not certain. The printed "Chri-" and "sti" at the end form one word split by the line end. The page has no separate footnote text; the bracketed line after the text is only a repeated marginal reading, so it is not a foot note. Printed errors left as printed.
